specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** place-the-site-in-its-era
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Built
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** apply
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the chapter's nine period boundaries to assign each of 15 sites and objects on the trip to the period in which it was built, with at least 12 of 15 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** historical timeline, BCE and CE dating, the nine periods and their dates, and the idea that a period name tells when, not always who (all defined in the chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each card, the learner assigns it to one of eight period bins (the Modern era is not used). An assignment is correct when it matches the Correct period column in Content. Mastery is 12 of 15 correct on the first attempt. Reading a card's description is not evidence; the committed assignment is. **Misconceptions:** (1) A period name always names the builder (the Palace of the Grand Master is "Byzantine" by date but was built by crusader knights). (2) A rebuilt or reconstructed monument belongs to the date of its reconstruction (the Stoa of Attalos was rebuilt in the 1950s but is Hellenistic). (3) Everything at Troy is from the time of the Trojan War. (4) The Iron Age left nothing to see. **Instructional Rationale:** Applying date boundaries to new cases is an Apply-level skill that improves with practice and immediate feedback. Each card gives a construction date and a short description, so the learner must use the period boundaries rather than recognize famous names; the two "trap" cards force the distinction between period and builder, and between original and reconstruction. **Content:** Period bins (with the boundaries the learner must apply): Bronze Age (c. 3200–1100 BCE); Iron Age (c. 1100–800 BCE); Archaic Period (c. 800–480 BCE); Classical Period (480–323 BCE); Hellenistic Period (323–31 BCE); Roman Period (31 BCE–330 CE); Byzantine Period (330–1453 CE); Ottoman Period (1453–1922 CE). Cards, presented in shuffled order: | # | Card text shown to the learner | Built | Correct period | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | The first palace at Knossos, Crete | c. 1900 BCE | Bronze Age | 1900 BCE falls between 3200 and 1100 BCE; the Minoans were a Bronze Age civilization. | | 2 | The gold "Mask of Agamemnon" from Mycenae, now in Athens | c. 1550–1500 BCE | Bronze Age | It is Mycenaean and about three centuries older than any date proposed for the Trojan War. | | 3 | The walls of Troy VI | c. 1750–1300 BCE | Bronze Age | Troy VI is a Late Bronze Age city; not everything at Troy is from the time of the Trojan War, but this layer is close. | | 4 | Painted jars from graves in the Kerameikos cemetery, Athens | c. 1000 BCE | Iron Age | 1000 BCE falls in the Iron Age (c. 1100–800 BCE); people kept living, and burying their dead, even without writing. | | 5 | The archaic Temple of Artemis at Ephesus | Begun c. 550 BCE | Archaic Period | 550 BCE falls between 800 and 480 BCE. | | 6 | The Athenian Treasury at Delphi | c. 500–490 BCE | Archaic Period | It was built before 480 BCE, so it is Archaic even though it looks Classical. | | 7 | The Parthenon on the Acropolis of Athens | 447–432 BCE | Classical Period | 447–432 BCE falls between 480 and 323 BCE. | | 8 | The Colossus of Rhodes (nothing survives) | Completed c. 280 BCE | Hellenistic Period | 280 BCE falls between 323 and 31 BCE. | | 9 | The Stoa of Attalos in the Athenian Agora, rebuilt in the 1950s | c. 150 BCE | Hellenistic Period | It was first built by King Attalos II of Pergamon around 150 BCE; a modern reconstruction keeps the period of the original. | | 10 | The Library of Celsus, Ephesus | Early 2nd century CE | Roman Period | The early 2nd century CE falls between 31 BCE and 330 CE. | | 11 | Hadrian's Arch, Athens | 131 CE | Roman Period | 131 CE falls between 31 BCE and 330 CE. | | 12 | Hagia Sophia, Istanbul | 537 CE | Byzantine Period | 537 CE falls between 330 and 1453 CE. | | 13 | The Palace of the Grand Master, Rhodes, built by crusader knights | 14th century CE | Byzantine Period | By date it falls in the Byzantine period (330–1453), even though it was built by the Knights Hospitaller, not by Byzantines: a period name tells when, not always who. | | 14 | Topkapı Palace, Istanbul | Begun 1459 CE | Ottoman Period | 1459 falls between 1453 and 1922 CE. | | 15 | The Süleymaniye Mosque, Istanbul | 1550–1557 CE | Ottoman Period | 1550–1557 falls between 1453 and 1922 CE. | **Provenance:** Dates for cards 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, and 13 are stated in this chapter's prose (sections "Archaeology," "The Minoan Civilization," "The Archaic Period," "The Classical Period," "The Hellenistic Period," "The Roman Empire," "The Byzantine Period," and "Putting It Together"). Dates for cards 2 (Mask of Agamemnon), 4 (Kerameikos Protogeometric burials), 6 (Athenian Treasury), 9 (Stoa of Attalos), 11 (Arch of Hadrian), 14 (Topkapı Palace), and 15 (Süleymaniye Mosque) are standard dates from each monument's Wikipedia article; the generator must check each against that article and keep the period assignment only if the checked date still falls inside it. **Rules:** A card whose date range lies entirely inside one period belongs to that period. "c." dates are treated as their stated number. A card dated "early 2nd century CE" or "14th century CE" belongs to the period containing that whole century. A boundary year belongs to the period it begins (480 BCE is Classical, 1453 CE is Ottoman). The Modern era bin is not shown because no card needs it. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the first card and the eight period bins in timeline order. 2. The learner assigns the card to a bin. The card's correctness and the Why text appear, and the card settles into its correct bin. 3. The learner presses Next for the next card, until all 15 are placed. 4. At the end, the learner sees all 15 cards sorted in their correct bins along the timeline, with the cards they missed marked. 5. The learner should notice that the two trap cards (13 and 9) turn on "when built" rather than "who built" or "when rebuilt." **Feedback:** Fifteen cards, shuffled once at the start, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: ." plus the Why text. Incorrect: "Not quite: this belongs in the ." plus the Why text. The correct bin is shown after every answer. A running score "Correct: n of 15" is shown. At the end: "12 or more: you can place the route in time" or "Fewer than 12: review the 24-hour clock table and try again." A Restart button reshuffles the cards and clears the score. **Starting State:** Eight empty bins labeled with period names and dates, one card showing "The first palace at Knossos, Crete — built c. 1900 BCE" (or whichever card the shuffle puts first), and the prompt "Which period was this built in?" **Chapter Anchors:** Nine periods with the dates in the 24-hour clock table (eight used here). Hagia Sophia completed 537 CE. The Palace of the Grand Master in Rhodes was built by crusader knights in the 1300s and falls in the Byzantine period by date. Parthenon 447–432 BCE. Colossus completed c. 280 BCE. Knossos first palace c. 1900 BCE. Troy VI c. 1750–1300 BCE.
